raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year on my 10.1 mu. I'm 66 now, been at this since I was a boy, so I know what works on my ground. My wife helps me but she's not young either, and the children are off working in town — they come back at busy times but I can't count on them for the day-to-day. So whatever I plan has to be something the two of us can handle, with a bit of hired help and machinery at the hard times.

**How I split the land**

I've got four crops to fit in 10.1 mu. Same split as the last few years because it works:

- **Wheat–maize double cropping: 5 mu.** This is my food crop and my anchor. I get two harvests a year off these fields. The government's been steady on the wheat minimum price, and I save my own wheat for us to eat. Maize I sell or keep for chickens.
- **Cotton: 3 mu.** Cotton pays better per mu than grain if the year is good, and I've grown it my whole life — our village in Quzhou is cotton country. But picking is hard on my back now. I'll hire a few people in October.
- **Stevia (甜叶菊): 2.1 mu.** The contracting company comes to our village — they give us seedlings and buy the dry leaf. It's fiddly work but the price per mu is better than wheat. My wife handles most of the weeding on this plot.

I'm not putting all my eggs in one basket. If cotton prices drop or bollworm is bad, I still have the grain. If wheat has a bad spring, stevia and cotton carry me.

---

**Wheat (already in the ground since last October)**

The wheat went in on October 10th last fall after the maize came off. I used Jimai-22 again — it's what most of us grow, yields well, and I can save seed. For the base fertilizer I broadcast 40 kg of 15-15-15 compound per mu before sowing, same as always.

Now it's April, wheat is at jointing. Looks decent — not the best color, a bit yellowish in the low spot of the east field. I'll topdress about 10 kg of urea per mu with the first spring irrigation, maybe 12 kg on the yellow patch. The extension fellow at the township station tells us 15 kg N/mu total is enough, but I've always done a bit more and I get 450 kg/mu in a good year. Last year I got 430, which is fine.

I'll irrigate 3 times: jointing now, then booting, then grain-filling if it's dry. Water from my tube well, about 30 yuan per time per mu in electricity. If it rains good in May I might skip the third one.

Herbicide I sprayed back in March — tribenuron for the broadleaf weeds, cost me about 15 yuan/mu. No pest spraying needed yet unless I see aphids at heading.

Expecting around 450 kg/mu this year. Harvest first week of June, right before the heat.

---

**Maize (planting mid-June, right after wheat)**

As soon as wheat is combined, I've got maybe 5-7 days to get maize in. I hire the neighbor's no-till seeder — he runs it right through the wheat stubble. Costs me 25 yuan/mu for the custom planting but it saves me two days of plowing and I'd never finish on time otherwise. At my age I'm not going to argue with a machine that works.

I use Zhengdan-958, hybrid seed, about 60 yuan/mu. Plant 4,500 plants per mu, which is what the book says and what my neighbor does.

Fertilizer: I'll put 30 kg of compound 15-15-15 down with the planter, then topdress 15 kg urea per mu at the big flare leaf stage (about knee-high). That's around 16 kg N/mu total. Maize is hungry for N, especially on my east field which is sandier.

Irrigation usually once or twice if July-August are dry — maize hits tasseling around end of July, that's when it really needs water. If the monsoon rains come good, I don't irrigate at all.

Atrazine + acetochlor pre-emergence for weeds, about 20 yuan/mu. Might need to spray for corn borer in August — I watch for it.

Last year I got 510 kg/mu maize. Expecting similar, maybe 500 this year.

---

**Cotton (planting now, late April)**

Cotton is my money crop but also my headache. I've got 3 mu in the southern plot — sandier soil, drains well, which cotton likes.

I plant mid-to-late April once the soil is warm. I use transplants from the village nursery for part of it and direct seed the rest — transplants give me an earlier start. Using the improved variety Luyanmian-21 or whatever the agro-shop has that's Bt (worm-resistant). Seed runs about 100 yuan/mu.

Base fertilizer: 40 kg compound 15-15-15 before planting. Then I topdress urea at squaring and bolling — about 10 kg each time, so maybe 13-14 kg N/mu total. Cotton doesn't need as much N as maize but the timing matters — too much late and the plant grows too tall and doesn't set bolls.

Pesticide is where cotton costs add up. With Bt cotton, bollworm isn't as bad as it used to be, but I still spray 3-4 times through the season for aphids, mites, and later-season worms. Budget maybe 60-80 yuan/mu for pesticide.

Irrigation 2 times, at squaring and flowering. No more — too much water late makes the bolls rot.

The picking is the hard part. Two pickings in September-October, maybe three. My wife and I can't do 3 mu by ourselves anymore, so I hire 3-4 women from the village for 5-6 days, maybe 400 yuan total. Then I take it to the ginner.

I'm hoping for 250 kg lint per mu. Last year I got 240.

---

**Stevia (planting April-May)**

The company delivered the seedlings last week — I got transplants for 2.1 mu. We'll finish planting this coming week, me and my wife and one daughter who's coming home for a few days.

Stevia doesn't need a lot of fertilizer — the company specifically tells us not to over-fertilize because it hurts the leaf sweetener quality. I put 20 kg compound 15-15-15 per mu at planting, then one light urea topdress of about 5 kg/mu in July. So about 8 kg N/mu total, which is less than any of my other crops.

Weed control is mostly by hand — no herbicide because the company wants clean leaf. That's my wife's main job through May and June.

Irrigation 2-3 times through the summer, whenever it looks dry.

Two cuts: first in early August, second in October. The company comes to collect the dried leaf and pays by weight. Last year I got about 250 kg dry leaf per mu total across the two cuts — that's where the real money was.

---

**Cash, labor, and what keeps me up at night**

Rough budget for inputs: 
- Wheat ~2,000 yuan on 5 mu (mostly topdress fertilizer and irrigation now)
- Maize ~1,700 yuan on 5 mu (coming in June)  
- Cotton ~1,400 yuan on 3 mu plus picking labor
- Stevia ~1,000 yuan on 2.1 mu

That's about 6,100 yuan in cash inputs for the year. I've got some saved from last year's stevia sale, and my son sends a bit home. I don't take out loans — never have.

Labor is my real worry, more than money. Two old people can't do cotton picking and stevia cutting and maize harvest all in the same September-October. I'll spend maybe 600-700 yuan on hired help at the peak times. Worth it.

What scares me this year: a late spring frost on the wheat (we had one in 2023, I lost 80 kg/mu), or too little rain in May before the wheat fills. And cotton prices — they've been poor the last few years. If they drop more I might cut back cotton next year, but this year's crop is already committed.
